## MiniMax Music 3

A music generation model by MiniMax that creates complete songs up to 5 minutes long with stable structure and high audio quality. Two inputs drive it: **Caption** (structured music description: style, mood, vocals, arrangement) and **Lyrics** (with `[intro]` `[verse]` `[chorus]` `[bridge]` `[outro]` tags controlling song structure).

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Caption | Music description. Write it in three sections — Global Metadata → Vocal Details → Arrangement. The more specific, the closer the result. |
| Lyrics | Song lyrics + section tags. Tags are the only executable structural instructions; the lyric text itself only conveys mood. |
| max_duration | Target song length in seconds (default 120 = 2 minutes; the model supports up to ~300 s / 5 minutes). Longer songs take more time and VRAM. |
| seed | Random seed for the generation. Keep it fixed to reproduce the same song; change it to get a different take. |
| Model files | diffusion model / text encoder / VAE.|
| Tiled decode | Decode the audio VAE in overlapping tiles to drastically cut VRAM usage — helpful for long songs on low-VRAM GPUs. Slightly slower, with a small risk of seams at tile boundaries; turn it off on high-VRAM GPUs for the best quality. |

### Prompt Writing Guide

You can find an official [Music Caption Rewriter Skill here](https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-Music3)

### Global Metadata

A dark, forceful K-pop girl-group title track combining dance-pop, electropop, and restrained trap-pop elements at 128 BPM. The emotional curve begins with controlled menace and whispered anticipation, becomes increasingly confident through the verses and rising pre-choruses, then erupts into a large, choreography-ready chorus. The second half grows more confrontational through a compact rap and industrial dance break, briefly exposes emotional resolve in the bridge, and finishes with a maximal, triumphant final chorus. Use a polished, high-impact contemporary pop mix with a wide stereo image, tight transient control, deep distorted sub-bass, cold synthesizer colors, and crisp metallic highs. Keep the production dark and regal rather than horror-like. Avoid cute styling, guitar-led rock, extended rap sections, and acoustic or retro-disco character.

### Vocal Details

Use a four-to-five-member female vocal group with clearly differentiated but cohesive voices. Alternate members during the verses: low mezzo-soprano lines should sound cool, close, and controlled, while lighter voices add clipped responses and breathy tension. Build the pre-choruses through ascending melodic delivery, increasingly dense harmonies, and restrained ad-libs. The choruses should use powerful full-group unison, stacked octave and third harmonies, and sharply articulated chant responses suitable for synchronized stage choreography. Deliver the second verse as a short, dry, percussive female rap without changing the song into a rap track. Use close whispered layers in the intro and outro, a vulnerable but steady bridge lead, and one clean high belt before the final chorus. Keep verse effects narrow and intimate; widen chorus layers with moderate plate reverb and short delays. Apply distortion or glitch processing only to selected chant fragments and transition words.

### Arrangement

Open with a filtered sub pulse, distant cold pad, reversed metallic swell, and whispered group texture. Verse 1 introduces a sparse syncopated electronic beat, low distorted 808 accents, and short minor-tonality synth stabs, leaving generous space around each member. The pre-chorus adds rolling hi-hats, rising noise, a tightening snare pattern, and an ascending arpeggiator while briefly reducing the sub before the drop. The chorus lands with a heavy four-on-the-floor kick reinforced by trap percussion, a wide saw-bass layer, metallic impacts, stacked claps, and a blunt two-part synth hook. Strip the post-chorus to bass, kick, vocal chops, and group chants for clear choreography accents.

Verse 2 shifts to a half-time trap feel with sliding 808 notes, dry snares, rapid hi-hat turns, and minimal industrial clicks under the rap. Rebuild the second pre-chorus and chorus with thicker backing vocals and additional upper synth layers. The dance break removes the harmonic pad and centers distorted 808 bends, mechanical percussion, hard stops, and processed group chants. For the bridge, cut the drums almost completely, retain a low atmospheric drone and sparse glassy keys, then grow through vocal harmonies and a rising impact into the high note. The final chorus restores every rhythmic and synth layer, adds counter-melody, extra ad-libs, and larger stereo percussion. End by abruptly removing the beat, leaving one whispered phrase, a decaying sub hit, and a hard stop rather than a fade.
